title: Microcommitments vs Burst Capacity — Hiring & Pricing Sensitivity Slate
content:
Purpose:
Run preliminary budgeting + headcount phasing for two commercial posture options we expect to present to Sales and Product: (A) Microcommitments (low-dollar monthly committed tiers sold broadly) vs (B) Pay-as-you-go with Burst Capacity (small reserved pool + on-demand burst).

Key questions this sheet answers (high level):
- At what usage mix / price delta do microcommitments improve 12-month gross margin vs pure burst?
- How does headcount (sales, SRE, support) scale in each option? Where are the biggest marginal costs?
- What are the break-even points to recommend an incentivized microcommitment product vs an add-on burst offering?

Assumptions (base case):
- Forecast horizon: 12 months (FY27 planning window).
- Billing unit: 1K tokens equivalent (generation + context).
- Base hosted unit cost (infrastructure + infra opex) = $0.006 per 1K tokens (current measured run-rate with batching & caching).
- On-demand burst premium multiplier = 2.4x base unit cost (due to autoscale cold-starts, multi-region redundancy, preemptible delta).
- Microcommitment discount to list = 18% (applied to unit price for committed tokens).
- Sales uplift for committed customers = +12% ARR expansion rate vs payg (due to stickiness and prepay).
- Average committed contract size (micro) = $9k/mo net ARR.
- Customer mix scenarios: Low-commitment adoption: 20% committed / 80% burst; Balanced: 45% / 55%; High-commitment adoption: 70% / 30%.

Scenario tables (summary view, monthly run-rate):
| Scenario | Committed % | Monthly tokens (m) | Rev per 1K (commit) | Rev per 1K (burst) | Avg gross unit cost | Revenue ($k/mo) | Infra cost ($k/mo) | Gross margin % | Incremental HC FTEs | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Low-commit | 20% | 120 | $0.0082 | $0.0123 | $0.0076 | 1,200 | 912 | 24.0 | +2 (support) | small commit adoption, lots of on-demand churn |
| Balanced | 45% | 140 | $0.0082 | $0.0123 | $0.0070 | 1,636 | 980 | 40.1 | +4 (2SRE, 1support, 1sales eng) | target mix for balanced offering |
| High-commit | 70% | 160 | $0.0082 | $0.0123 | $0.0066 | 2,162 | 1,056 | 51.1 | +6 (4sales, 2SRE) | enterprise-scale commit adoption |

Notes on table inputs:
- Revenue per 1K (commit) = list_price * (1 - 0.18). We model list_price = $0.010 per 1K in base retail.
- Revenue per 1K (burst) = list_price * (1 + burst_premium) => $0.010 * 1.23 ~ $0.0123 in our base case (we assume 23% surcharge passed to customer; internal cost multiplier is 2.4x).
- Avg gross unit cost accounts for capacity amortization, reserved discounting, and ops FTE allocation for serving runtime (blended).

Headcount phasing (12-month snapshot, incremental hires by quarter):
- Baseline (org needs regardless of product): Finance(2), Legal(1), Platform eng(8), Applied ML(6), DX(3). These are already budgeted.
- Incremental hires (option-dependent, shown as cumulative by quarter):
  - Microcommitments product (Option A): Q1: +1 Sales AE, Q2: +1 Sales AE, Q2: +1 Sales Engineer, Q3: +1 Support IC, Q4: +1 Revenue Ops. Total incremental = +5 FTE.
  - Burst-capacity add-on (Option B): Q1: +1 SRE (autoscale focus), Q2: +1 Infra Eng (costing & spot optimization), Q3: +1 Support IC, Q4: +1 Solutions Engineer (on-call for peaks). Total incremental = +4 FTE.

Headcount cost assumptions (loaded):
- Sales AE loaded = $220k/year (comp + burden).
- Sales Engineer = $210k/year.
- SRE = $240k/year.
- Infra Eng = $230k/year.
- Support IC = $120k/year.
- Revenue Ops = $150k/year.

12-month P&L delta (incremental view vs baseline, ARR-normalized):
- Option A (microcommitments): incremental HC cost (5 FTE) = $1.05M/year. Estimated incremental gross margin improvement vs burst = +$1.28M/year (driven by committed pricing + expansion). Net delta = +$230k (favorable).
- Option B (burst): incremental HC cost (4 FTE) = $0.88M/year. Estimated incremental margin improvement = +$0.9M/year (less uplift). Net delta = +$20k (marginally favorable).

Sensitivity analysis (three levers):
1) Commit discount (12% to 25%) — lower discount improves gross margin for Option A and shifts break-even earlier.
2) Burst internal cost multiplier (1.8x to 3.0x) — higher multiplier penalizes Option B; benefit to commitments grows non-linearly.
3) Committed adoption rate (20% to 70%) — adoption dominates outcomes; small increases in adoption disproportionately favor Option A.

Critical break-even examples (assuming base volumes above):
- If commit discount <= 14% and committed adoption >= 40% -> Option A outperforms Option B by >$500k/year.
- If burst internal multiplier <2.0 and committed adoption stays <=25% -> Option B slightly preferred (lower HC overhead, simpler ops).

Risks / open questions:
- Sales packaging: Microcommitments require heavier contract & billing ops (invoicing cadence, refund/accounting rules). Legal/RevOps effort may be front-loaded beyond our HC estimates.
- Metering complexity: mixed workloads and burst fallbacks complicate invoicing reconciliation and may require engineering instrumentation (add 0.5-1 infra FTE in worst case).
- Customer behavior: committed customers may shift to different models if we enforce strict prefix caching rules; need product gating experiments.

Recommended near-term experiments (next 90 days):
1) Pilot microcommitment SKU with 10 pilot accounts (discount 15%, 6-month minimum). Track retention, expansion, and per-token effective cost.
2) Run a controlled stress test on the burst autoscaler to measure real-world burst cost multiplier (goal: refine 2.4x assumption).
3) Build a simple billing parity report (daily reconciliation of billed tokens across commit vs burst paths) to estimate instrumentation work and detect leakage.

Appendix: quick sensitivity table (Net delta vs baseline across commit discount and burst multiplier, values show annual net delta in $k):
| Commit discount | Burst mult 1.8x | Burst mult 2.4x | Burst mult 3.0x |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 12% | 410 | 290 | 160 |
| 15% | 330 | 210 | 80 |
| 18% (base) | 230 | 120 | -10 |
| 22% | 120 | 30 | -110 |
| 25% | 60 | -40 | -200 |

- This is intentionally conservative on adoption and conservative on uplift. If Sales returns stronger signal from initial conversations, re-run with higher ARR expansion assumptions.
- The sheet is a draft for Finance + GTM alignment; please leave inline comments or link to JIRA FIN-897 for tracked changes.
